title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Medical equipment cleaning (external only)
audience: Owners and supervisors of businesses that clean the external surfaces of medical equipment in clinics and care settings, under a facility's written instruction, who write offers for facility managers.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer for external equipment cleaning with a clear outcome, time frame and conditions, that does not promise any reprocessing or clinical result
Identify the friction and risk the facility carries, including the release of equipment and access, and reduce them
Price the offer on scope and risk, and check the price against your own cost and time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer for external equipment
instruction.body: 'We clean your medical equipment' is too broad, and it may suggest work you are not authorised to do. 'We clean the external surfaces of the trolleys and bed frames named on your written list, on the day the facility releases them, and sign the list for each item' is an offer. The facility buys a checkable result inside a defined scope. It does not buy reprocessing, disinfection of reusable devices, or any decision about whether an item is fit for patient use. Those decisions stay with the facility's clinical and reprocessing staff.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome, named by item and by surface; a defined time frame that fits the facility's release process; what the facility must provide, such as the written list, the release sign-off and access; the certainty you provide, such as a signed item list and a visit log; and the risk you carry, such as a re-clean commitment for listed items you can keep. Put the scope and exclusions in writing. Exclude any equipment the facility has classed as critical or semi-critical, and any internal or invasive device, unless the facility's own team does that work. A written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction for the facility
instruction.body: Equipment moves between rooms and between clinical teams. Agree how items are booked, moved and released, who signs for them, and where they are kept while clean. Fewer decisions for the facility usually supports a higher price, because the facility pays for a reliable hand-off.

instruction.heading: Guarantees, claims and a fix-first promise
instruction.body: Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services. An optional workmanship warranty sits on top of those guarantees and cannot remove them, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). A fix-first promise, where you re-clean a listed item that fails your checklist at no charge, fits the expectation that a business gets a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (Consumer Victoria, 13 October 2023). Do not claim that equipment is sterile, disinfected or fit for patient use. The research found no manufacturer or TGA source on external cleaning, so do not make any claim that depends on one.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value, with GST shown
instruction.body: Price from the scope and the risk, then check the price against your cost and time. The research found no medical-equipment pricing source, so the rate must come from your own records. Misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, 15 July 2026), and the quote should show one clear total with a statement of whether GST is included (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026). Price any extra item or extra movement of equipment in writing before the work starts. Business Queensland suggests charging added costs at cost plus 15 per cent; that is one source's suggestion, not a medical-equipment benchmark.

procedure: Write the outcome as the named items and surfaces on the facility's written list, in one sentence the facility manager would repeat.
Set a time frame that fits the facility's release process, and record how often you have met similar windows.
List what the facility must provide, including the written list, the release sign-off and access, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a signed item list and a visit log.
Decide the re-clean commitment for listed items that fail, and check that you can deliver it.
Price from scope and risk, check the rate against cost and time, then show the total with its GST status.

workedExamples.situation: A clinic's current cleaner charges by the hour and cannot say which items are covered. The practice manager wants the external surfaces of trolleys, cabinets and chairs cleaned between clinic sessions, and does not want any reprocessing.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the offer name, what should it leave out, and how should it be priced?
workedExamples.reasoning: The offer names each item type on the clinic's written list, the surfaces to be cleaned, the time window agreed with the clinic and a signed list for each session. It leaves out reprocessing, disinfection of reusable devices, invasive devices and any decision to release equipment for patient use, and says those stay with the clinic. The signed list records that shared equipment is cleaned with detergent between uses, and that disinfection is used where indicated, as the facility's instruction defines it. A surface barrier does not replace cleaning (NHMRC 2019 edition as read, recommendations 10 and 11; check the current version). The price comes from the cost of the scope, the time and the risk, with GST status shown. The research found no source for medical-equipment prices, so no figure is given in this example.

commonErrors.error: Promising a result the cleaner cannot control, such as sterility or fitness for patient use
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the external cleaning you deliver against the facility's list, and leave clinical and reprocessing decisions to the facility.

commonErrors.error: Quoting without exclusions for critical or semi-critical equipment and internal devices
commonErrors.prevention: List what is excluded, and confirm in writing that the facility's own team handles it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. Equipment that a facility classes as critical or semi-critical, and any reprocessing or release decision, sit with the facility and are outside this course. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority, and does not replace the manufacturer's cleaning instructions, which the facility supplies where it has them.

qualityStandard: Every offer names the items, surfaces, exclusions and facility inputs, and is checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with item scope, exclusions, time window and GST status; the signed item list; and the cost and time check used to set the price.
summary: An external equipment offer promises a checkable result on a named list, with a time frame and a fair fix-first commitment.
Price from scope and risk; the research has no medical-equipment price, so use your own records and show GST status.
